answer.rationale: Three pressures compete for the single experiment slot: competitor pricing erosion, activation decline, and onboarding completion decline. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given the competitive threat, but it optimizes for price-sensitive acquisition, which risks attracting lower-quality, low-LTV accounts and entrenching a race-to-the-bottom dynamic that conflicts with the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue — that risk was never measured in the original test. In contrast, the onboarding and activation declines are internal funnel-health problems directly addressed by two prior validated interventions (signup field reduction and onboarding shortening), both of which produced durable, quality-neutral gains in activation and time-to-value without evidence of harming revenue quality. Because these two memories overlap in mechanism (reducing friction in the early funnel) and both bear on the current onboarding-completion drop, I want to pull their original archived records to confirm effect size, population, and whether any tradeoffs (e.g., lost qualification data from shorter signup forms) were noted before committing the one available experiment to a combined simplified-onboarding treatment. This path is lower-risk, addresses metrics currently in active decline, and avoids gambling the week's only experiment on a pricing move whose downstream revenue-quality effects are unverified.
